tool.title: Candidate translations — LibreTranslate / Argos
tool.description: LibreTranslate (self-hosted) or its engine Argos Translate (offline, installed packages), an open machine-translation model run locally, proposes a translation for each string and appends them to the catalogue's candidates sidecar with `source.kind: open-mt` and the Argos package or server. Seeds an empty `msgstr` with the first candidate, fuzzy.

install.cli: pip install argostranslate (offline), or pip install libretranslate

inputs.name: catalogue
inputs.description: The `.po` catalogue to propose translations for.

outputs.name: candidates
outputs.description: `<locale>/<catalogue>.candidates.json` (`translation-candidates/v1`), appended to; and the `.po`, where an empty `msgstr` now holds the first candidate marked `#, fuzzy`.

selection.when: An open engine that can run as a local service or fully offline, for a team that already hosts one or cannot install PyTorch.
selection.limits: Quality below OPUS-MT on most pairs, context-blind like it, and a public instance rate-limits and sees the text. Prose that needs context: `translation-candidates-agent`.
selection.cost: A small Python package and about 100 MB per language package offline, or one container; a public instance needs an API key.

remedies.none: Run it locally instead: `argostranslate` offline, or the `libretranslate/libretranslate` container on localhost. The public instance is a convenience, not a dependency.

$comment.comment: Today the same engines fill catalogues through `translation:machine-fill` (`translation-machine-fill`, cat-harness#1329), which writes the `msgstr` directly, fuzzy, with no candidates sidecar. This node is the candidates form of the engine: provisional until the sidecar writer and its checkout-script key land, at which point `invoke.shell` names it and `manual` goes.
